newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PEACEKEEPERS TO START LEAVING ALBANIA MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PEACEKEEPERS TO START LEAVING ALBANIA MONDAY.

text.p: Greek peacekeepers participating in the Italian-led multi-national force in Albania will withdraw from the troubled Balkan country between July 21 and August 8, Greece's defence ministry said on Thursday.
The 11-nation force of 7,000 soldiers, deployed in April to help distribute aid and to ensure smooth elections on June 29 and July 6, is due to withdraw by August 12.
Greece, concerned about the violence that gripped its northern neighbour in March, sent about 800 soldiers to participate in Operation Alba (Italian for dawn).
"The Greek force will return gradually ... by boat and by road," the ministry said in a statement.
Violence erupted in Europe's poorest country when popular get-rich-quick savings funds collapsed, leaving investors destitute.

After two rounds of elections, the multinational protection force began its gradual withdrawl on Wednesday, with Romanian troops leaving the southern town of Gjirokaster for the Adriatic port of Durres.
